desc:
The array nums contains distinct positive integers. A subset of its values is divisible if for every two numbers a and b in the subset, either a divides b or b divides a.

Return the number of elements in the largest divisible subset. A subset with one element is always divisible. For nums = [4, 8, 10, 240] the answer is 3 (4, 8, 240).
constraints: All values of nums are distinct
hints: Sort the array first. In a sorted divisible subset, which pairs do you really need to check?
If a < b < c and a divides b and b divides c, then a divides c automatically. So a divisible subset is just a chain in which each element divides the next.
Let size[i] be the longest chain ending at the i-th smallest value: size[i] = 1 + max size[j] over j < i with nums[i] % nums[j] == 0. The answer is the maximum size[i].
editorial: Divisibility is transitive: if a divides b and b divides c then a divides c. After sorting ascending, a subset is divisible exactly when each element divides the next one in sorted order; then every earlier element divides every later one by transitivity. That turns the problem into a longest-chain problem, just like longest increasing subsequence with 'greater than' replaced by 'is a multiple of'.

Define size[i] as the largest divisible subset whose biggest element is nums[i] (in sorted order). Then size[i] = 1 + max(size[j]) over earlier j with nums[i] % nums[j] == 0, or 1 if there is none. The result is the maximum of all size[i]. The cost is O(n log n) for sorting plus O(n2) for the double loop, with O(n) memory.

Because the values are distinct, a chain always has strictly increasing elements, so sorting never breaks a valid subset. (To print the subset itself, remember for each i the j that gave the maximum and walk back from the best index.)
